h1: Dener tube lasers — E-FTL and FTL, Ø0.3″ to 25.2″, bars to 39.4 ft, 3 to 20 kW
intro: Dener's tube lasers are the premium line of NovoTech's tube laser section: built in Kayseri, Turkey, with servo chucks, Precitec heads and 3 to 20 kW sources, and backed by Dener Canada parts in Mississauga, ON, Canada. The E-FTL is the fast machine for the sizes most fabricators use — railings, frames, furniture, trailers, exhaust: four chuck sizes from Ø0.3″ to 13.8″, servo axes accelerating at 1 G to 394 ft/min and ±0.05 mm repeatability on 7, 9 or 12 m bars. The FTL is built for weight: structural tube, pipe and beams to Ø25.2″ and 12 m bars of 2,600 kg — 12,000 kg on the long-bed 250 — with ±0.1 mm on the large chucks and a 5-axis bevel head for weld preparations. Both load from a bundle automatically, support the tube as it is cut, nest parts along the bar from STEP / IGES models and unload finished pieces. Installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.a: The E-FTL is the fast machine for the sizes most fabricators use — railings, frames, furniture, trailers, exhaust — Ø0.3″ to 13.8″, accelerating at 1 G and running 394 ft/min on the small chucks. The FTL is built for weight: structural tube and pipe to Ø25.2″ and 12 m bars of 2,600 kg, with ±0.1 mm repeatability on the large chucks. Both take the same 3 – 20 kW sources and bundle loaders.

The number is the largest round tube in millimetres: E-FTL 120 takes Ø0.3 – 4.7″, 180 to 7.1″, 250 to 9.8″ and 350 to 13.8″; FTL 250, 350, 500 and 640 take Ø0.6″ to 9.8, 13.8, 19.7 and 25.2″. Square and rectangular tube is limited by the diagonal, so a 350 chuck takes about 9.8″ square. Buy the chuck for the largest tube you cut regularly — a smaller chuck is faster and holds thin tube better — and the bar length (7, 9 or 12 m) for the stock you buy.

faq.q: Can it cut bevels and weld preparations?
faq.a: Yes — the 5-axis head on the FTL (optional on the E-FTL) tilts to ±45° so mitred corners, chamfers and weld preparations are cut in the same pass as the holes and copes; the tube arrives at the welding table ready to fit. The seam detector orients welded tube so the seam sits where the drawing puts it.

faq.q: How does Dener compare with the Senfeng value line?
faq.a: Dener's E-FTL and FTL are the premium machines — Turkish-built, 1 G servo chucks, Precitec heads, Dener Canada parts in Mississauga, ON, Canada. Senfeng's tube lasers are the value line: a 6 m two-chuck machine with a 1.5 kW source costs a fraction of a premium tube laser, and the range goes to zero-tailing three-chuck and four-chuck machines for 49 ft stock. The comparison and the capacity table for both lines are on the tube laser cutters overview.

A 7 m E-FTL needs about 20 m (65 ft) of length including the loader and unloader; a 12 m FTL about 30 m. 600 V 3-phase with the supplied transformer or 480 V, a chiller (included), assist gas and a dust collector. We lay the machine out for your building before you order.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
